- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. # Cold read — brief-032 version 2, round 2

Judge: cold-reviewer role (basis/roles/cold-reviewer.md v5), model claude-fable-5. Read: the brief alone, once, as the product authority. Annex and round 1 not opened.

## Verdict: findings

Nothing is marked in the text as an accepted tradeoff, so "tradeoffs-accepted" is not available. The brief is far better than its round-1 history entry suggests the first version was, and every ask is decidable at the level of "yes, proceed" — but several stumbles and one unintroduced-term cluster remain.

## Stumbles, in reading order

1. "session record (the conversation's own record)" — the gloss restates the term; I still do not know what a session record is as a thing in the system (a file? a typedef?). Minor; I could move on.

2. "composed of six sub-processes — three exist, two are new, one is new and small" — the count parses (3+2+1=6) but "new and small" is a size claim with no number (guideline rule 5: numbers over adjectives). Ask 1 later shows `backlog-ordering` as the small one, but the opening does not say which.

3. "a build plan of five batches, each screened once as a set" — then ask 2 says "Four screens, five blocks." The opening says every batch is screened once; the ask says one batch (B) is not screened separately. The opening contradicts the ask. The ask's own text ("B... screened with A, one hand-off") explains it, so this is a stumble, not a decidability failure — but I had to re-read.

4. "about five working sessions" — the one effort number in the brief; no unit for what a working session is (hours? a day?). I would want to know what I am spending. The annex is said to carry "the batch table with effort", which means the effort I need is not on the page.

5. Ask 1, `discovery-conversation`: "in a form — brainstorm first; interview and review of evidence later" — "form" is used as a coined term (three forms, per ask 3's "discovery forms beyond the three") but arrives here without saying it is a category of discovery. I counted: brainstorm, interview, review of evidence — three. The reader has to do that count to connect it to ask 3.

6. Ask 1, `initiative-check`: "the architect attaches feasibility and the decomposition, the designer usability" — "the designer" is a role I have not seen named in the six-role world I know (PM/PO/Architect). Not glossed; who fills it is not said. Same again in `feature-authoring` ("the designer adds criteria").

7. Ask 1, `initiative-check`: "whether to spend the appetite" — "appetite" is not introduced. I recognize it as Shape Up vocabulary, but the brief does not say so and does not say who sets it or where it is recorded.

8. Ask 1, `feature-authoring`: "(by ask; while shops are frozen, the PO's marked hypothesis stands in)" — "by ask" is opaque: co-produced by asking the shops? through a message? "marked hypothesis" is unintroduced — marked how, and where?

9. Ask 1, `po-output-check`: "on the first pass the initiative becomes `active`" — first pass of what? Of the check (i.e. the first feature that passes)? Ambiguous between "first attempt" and "first feature to pass".

10. Ask 1, `scenario-assignment` "(exists; draft)" — the other labels are "exists; amended" and "new". "exists; draft" is a third state that is not explained: does the batch D work amend it, approve it, or finish it?

11. Ask 1 evidence: "the 2026-08-27 system-read report found eight of ten hops in a feature's path undefined; each is now a named step" — good, numbered. But "the bet inside the check removes the review-conversation amendment the initiative typedef listed" is a sentence I cannot evaluate: I do not know what amendment the initiative typedef listed, so "removes" is evidence only to the author.

12. Ask 1 "*Default:* none." — I read this as "there is no default; silence does not approve". That is consistent with the opening ("Ask 1 gates the work"). Fine, but "none" could be read as "default is to do nothing" — one word ("gates; no default") would remove the ambiguity.

13. Ask 2: "the definitions already drafted (initiative and feature chains, assignment, PO guidelines, three typedef amendments) are approved with the batch that re-screens them in context, not separately" — this is the deferred-approval move the history entry mentions. It is a real commitment (block approval covers material I have not seen), placed under *Drafting default*. A drafting default is something the author may change without me; approval scope is not that. This should be under *Binds* or be its own ask. Guideline rule 4 concern.

14. Ask 2 evidence: "the last three days ran three rounds per definition" — a number, good; but the claim "cuts the reviewing" has no number against it (from N rounds to M screens). The reader who wants less per-artifact reviewing wants that figure.

15. Ask 3: "the `router` role that reconcile-and-close names" — `reconcile-and-close` is not introduced anywhere in the brief; `router` is not glossed. "the reconcile side, after assignment" in the same ask half-introduces "reconcile" but not the process name.

16. Ask 3: "discovery forms beyond the three" — see stumble 5; depends on the reader having counted.

17. Deferred: "Nothing further; the deferred approvals are inside ask 2." — the section then says there is something deferred (approvals) and that it is inside an ask. The typedef says deferrals are notes, never asks. Either these are deferrals (then they belong here as notes) or they are part of ask 2's binding (then say "None" here). As written the section contradicts itself in one line.

## Terms arriving before the brief explains them

- `session record` (gloss is circular)
- `form` as a category of discovery
- `the designer` (role)
- `appetite`
- `by ask` / `marked hypothesis`
- `first pass`
- `exists; draft` (status label)
- `reconcile-and-close`, `router`, `the reconcile side`
- `changelog` (ask 3: which changelog — the initiative's?)
- `the primer's first paragraph` (ask 2, batch E) — I know the primer exists as a reader of this shop, so this passes on shop vocabulary; noting it only because "first paragraph" as a deliverable is odd without saying what changes in it.

Process names in backticks (`discovery-conversation`, `initiative-check`, etc.) are introduced by their one-line descriptions and pass.

## Per-ask decidability

**Ask 1 — approve the model.** Confident on the shape: six named steps, each with an owner and an exit, and the states (`proposed`/`planned`/`active`/`cancelled`) form a visible path. Binds vs drafting default: stated ("these six and their hand-offs" / "prompts, caps, wording"). Gating: stated (gates; default none). Wobbly on two details: who "the designer" is, and what "by ask" co-production means during the freeze — I would approve with the six and ask those two as conditions.

**Ask 2 — build order and block approval.** Wobbly. Order A–E is decidable and I would accept it. Block approval is decidable in principle. What I cannot decide with confidence is the scope of the deferred-approval clause (stumble 13): approving ask 2 as written silently approves an unlisted set of already-drafted definitions on the day their batch screens. Binds vs drafting default: stated, but the split places the largest commitment on the default side. Gating: stated (defaults on silence). Effort: "about five working sessions" only; the per-batch effort is in the annex — a reader deciding the order without effort per batch is deciding blind on cost (fitness scenario 1, partial).

**Ask 3 — accept the exclusions.** Confident. Four exclusions, each with a reason ("none is on the path"), binds stated ("none is built in A–E"), default stated (accepted). Two of the four carry unglossed names (`router`, `reconcile-and-close`) but the decision — exclude them — does not depend on knowing what they are.

## Overload

Right-sized for one reading in length. The load is in ask 1's six lines, which carry role names, states, and parentheticals at once; the six lines are the model, so they belong on the page. What could be deferred: the parenthetical about the freeze in `feature-authoring`, and the "removes the review-conversation amendment" clause in the evidence — both speak to the author's history, not the reader's decision.

## Budgets

- Decision layer (The answer first + Asks): 534 words against ~400 — 34% over. The answer-first paragraph alone is 106 words. The overage sits in ask 1's six model lines (~190 words) and ask 2's batch list (~60 words). Is it justified by decidability? Mostly yes: the six lines are what ask 1 approves and the reader must see them to decide it; round 1 apparently faulted their absence. The batch list is also the object of ask 2. What is not justified: the ~50 words of author-history evidence in asks 1 and 2 (stumble 11, the "three rounds per definition" sentence) and the freeze parenthetical — trimming those brings the layer to ~480, which I would accept as the price of a model-approval brief.
- Whole (title through annex link): 582 words against ~1,500 — well under.

| 1 — decidable without the annex | Partial | Asks 1 and 3: yes. Ask 2: the per-batch effort is annex-only; the deferred-approval set is named by category, not listed. |

| 4 (Then) — each ask complete | Pass | All three carry recommendation (the "What you approve" statement), evidence, default. |
| 4 (And) — gating stated | Pass | "Ask 1 gates the work; asks 2 and 3 default on silence." |

## Top three changes

1. **Move the deferred-approval clause in ask 2 from *Drafting default* to *Binds*, and list what it covers** — name the definitions (or count them) that block approval will sweep in, so the reader knows what "approved with the batch" commits them to. Then make the Deferred section say "None."
2. **Gloss the six terms in one clause each**: the designer (who fills it), appetite (who sets it), marked hypothesis / by ask (what co-production is during the freeze), reconcile-and-close and router (one phrase: "the post-assignment process and the role it names"). Fix the circular "session record" gloss.
3. **Reconcile the opening with ask 2 and put a number on cost and saving**: change "each screened once as a set" to "four screens, five blocks"; state what a working session is or give effort per batch on the page; state the review reduction as a number ("from ~3 rounds per definition to 4 screens for N definitions").
